title: Music and media rights in numbers
heading: How far off is your gut?
intro: Eight real numbers about who earns what when songs and stories find an audience: streams, records, songs and books.
Every figure is real and sourced. Bet on how sure you are, not just on what you think.

outro.heading: Rights are where the money is.
paras: Behind every hit, old or new, there are contracts that decide who gets paid and who gets a say. The sums are often bigger, or smaller, than people expect.
Today, keep asking who holds which right, and why it matters to them.

questions.q: Mariah Carey's 'All I Want for Christmas Is You' came out in 1994. In which year did it first reach No. 1 in the UK?
questions.explain: December 2020, 26 years after release. Streaming brings the song back every winter, and it climbed a little higher each year until it reached the top.

questions.q: Spotify paid more than $11 billion to the music industry in 2025. Roughly how many artists generated more than $1 million each from it?
questions.sub: over 80% never had a global Top 50 hit
questions.explain: More than 1,500 (about 1,540), up from 460 in 2017, and more than 80% of them never had a song in Spotify's Global Daily Top 50. The money goes to rights holders (labels, publishers, distributors), who then pay artists under their own contracts.
questions.source: Spotify, Loud & Clear report, March 2026 (via Music Business Worldwide)

questions.q: Since 2024 a track on Spotify must reach a minimum number of streams in the previous 12 months before it earns any royalties at all. What is the minimum?
questions.explain: 1,000 streams a year. Spotify argued that tracks below it earned only a few cents, often too little ever to reach a payout, and that the money should go to other artists. Critics said it hit small artists hardest.
questions.source: Music Business Worldwide, November 2023 and April 2024

questions.q: In a 2023 US survey, people who had bought a vinyl record in the past year were asked about their equipment. What share did not own a record player?
questions.explain: About half. Many buyers treat a record as a souvenir, a poster or a way to support an artist, and listen to the music on a streaming service instead.

questions.q: How many hardback copies were in Bloomsbury's first print run of Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone in 1997?
questions.explain: Just 500, and about 300 of those went to libraries. Several publishers, reportedly a dozen, had turned the book down. A first-edition hardback can now sell for tens of thousands of pounds.

questions.q: Until a US court ruled in 2015 that its copyright claim was invalid, how much did a music publisher reportedly earn each year from 'Happy Birthday to You'?
questions.sub: a year, mostly from films and TV
questions.explain: About $2 million a year for Warner/Chappell, mainly from films, TV shows and adverts that used the song. After a judge ruled its claim invalid in September 2015, it agreed in 2016 to pay $14 million to settle the case, and the song is now free to use in the US.

questions.q: In 2024 Sony Music agreed to buy the rights to Queen's music catalogue. What was the deal widely reported to be worth?
questions.sub: the price was not officially confirmed
questions.explain: About £1 billion, reported as the biggest music catalogue deal ever. Investors pay for income they expect to last for decades: Queen's songs still earn from streams, films and adverts.
questions.source: Widely reported (e.g. Radio X, Hypebeast), June 2024

questions.q: Before buying back the original master recordings of her first six albums in May 2025, how many of them had Taylor Swift re-recorded and released as 'Taylor's Version'?
questions.explain: Four. The re-recordings gave fans versions she owned, and made the old masters less valuable to their owners. In May 2025 she bought the originals from the private equity firm Shamrock Capital.
